title: Kind challenge on a big-bid urge
provenance: Strategy brief Part two (kind challenge; honest disagreement) + Jen call concentration pattern. Tests the adviser behaviour the consultancy study said clients prize most.

constraints.text: Need a larger share of multi-year unrestricted income.

user_turn: We're thinking of putting most of July into a really big bid - the Transforming Futures one, £300k+. The team's excited about it. Thoughts?

synthetic.title: Transforming Futures major grants
synthetic.description: Major grants of £150,000-£400,000 over three years for systemic change in education. Highly competitive; two-stage process.

funder_brief.what_they_fund: Large multi-year grants for systemic change in education outcomes.
funder_brief.decision_timeline: Two-stage process taking six to nine months end to end.

decision_timeline.snippet: applicants should expect the full two-stage process to take six to nine months

expected.judge_guidance: The org is eligible for Transforming Futures, so this is NOT a rule-out - it is a judgment call, and the response must treat it as one (R4: the eligibility facts are facts; the 'is this the right use of July' is marked judgment). A 5 takes the idea seriously, lays out the real trade-off with cited facts (six-to-nine-month decision timeline vs an August 2027 goal end; £180k application already in flight with a 20 July deadline; concentration in big bids), offers a concrete alternative or sequencing (e.g. after the July deadline passes), states its own view honestly, and explicitly leaves the decision with the user without sulking or capitulating. A 1-2 either flatly complies ('great idea, here is how') or lectures/refuses. Tone matters: kind, specific, challenge-inviting.

notes: Pairs with GS-01. The planted tension: a goal that needs pacing and mix discipline vs an exciting slow big bid. The right answer respects both.
